hints: Focus on what colour tells you here, purple in the organic layer always means iodine, $\text{I}_2$, has dissolved in hexane.
Remember hexane floats on water, so the upper layer is hexane, and work out in which experiments $\text{I}_2$ is present either because it was added or because it was displaced.
Count both types together, the tubes where iodine was added but did not react plus the tubes where a more reactive halogen displaced iodine from iodide.
walkthrough:
**Identify what purple upper layer means**

Great start, let's decode the observation. Hexane is a non-polar organic solvent and is less dense than water, so it forms the upper layer.

Halogens dissolve much better in hexane and show clear colours: $\text{Cl}_2$ is very pale green, $\text{Br}_2$ is orange-brown, $\text{I}_2$ is purple-violet. So a purple upper layer means $\text{I}_2$ is present in the tube.

**Apply halogen displacement reactivity**

Now recall the reactivity order: $\text{Cl}_2 > \text{Br}_2 > \text{I}_2$. A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halide from solution.

$$\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{Br}^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cl}^- + \text{Br}_2$$
$$\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{I}^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cl}^- + \text{I}_2$$
$$\text{Br}_2 + 2\text{I}^- \rightarrow 2\text{Br}^- + \text{I}_2$$
Iodine cannot displace chloride or bromide, so experiments 7, 8 and 9 have no reaction.

**List where $\text{I}_2$ ends up**

Let's go through the table:
Experiment 3: $\text{Cl}_2$ displaces $\text{I}_2$ from $\text{I}^-$, so $\text{I}_2$ present.
Experiment 6: $\text{Br}_2$ displaces $\text{I}_2$ from $\text{I}^-$, so $\text{I}_2$ present.
Experiments 7, 8, 9: $\text{I}_2$ was added and stays as $\text{I}_2$ because no reaction occurs.

All other tubes contain only $\text{Cl}_2$ or $\text{Br}_2$, which give non-purple layers.

**Count the purple tubes**

That gives purple upper layers in experiments 3, 6, 7, 8 and 9.

That is $2 + 3 = 5$ test-tubes in total.

options.A: 1 is far too low. It ignores most sources of iodine. You may have counted only one displacement, perhaps experiment 3, and forgotten that bromine also displaces iodine and that added iodine itself stays purple when no reaction happens.
options.B: 2 is the classic trap. Experiments 3 and 6 do produce $\text{I}_2$ by displacement ($\text{Cl}_2$ + $\text{I}^-$ and $\text{Br}_2$ + $\text{I}^-$). But this forgets experiments 7, 8 and 9 where $\text{I}_2$ was added at the start and remains to colour the hexane purple.
options.C: 3 counts only the three tubes where iodine solution was added (7, 8, 9). This misses the key idea that iodine can also be formed in situ by displacement in experiments 3 and 6, which also give a purple hexane layer.
options.D: 5 is correct. Purple means $\text{I}_2$ in the upper hexane layer. $\text{I}_2$ is formed in experiment 3 and experiment 6 by displacement, and is already present with no reaction in experiments 7, 8 and 9. That is 5 tubes total.
